conditional_voice_coverage.qualification: Matched-chord voice categories project each voice onto complete chord keys appearing exactly once in both scores. Unmatched or ambiguous chords are excluded, so these categories alone cannot establish recognition quality.

across_measure_voice_coverage.qualification: Only adjacent measures on the same staff with one nonoverlapping local stream on each side in BOTH scores are scored. Local voice labels may change freely across the barline. The compared pair is the last complete group before the boundary and the first after it, retaining pitch, duration and grace identity. Multiple streams, empty measures and missing boundaries remain unscored; no pitch-distance or reused-label heuristic supplies continuity. This does not prove polyphonic voice identity across measures.

scope.events: Exact staff order, measure order, rational onset/duration, MIDI pitch/rest and grace status.
scope.chords: Actual serialized chord grouping, compared as complete pitch multisets; simultaneous independent voices stay separate.
scope.voices: Per-staff, per-measure ordered partitions and successive chord/rest edges; arbitrary labels excluded. Full categories include pitch/timing errors; matched-chord categories isolate voice membership over stated common anchors. Across-measure comparisons cover only jointly unambiguous single-stream boundaries, with explicit coverage and exclusions.
scope.measures: Nominal meters, occupied/forward extent, irregular/implicit markers and part/staff membership; printed measure numbers excluded.
scope.slurs: Reciprocal MuseScore chord locations versus paired MusicXML slur numbers. Full musical chord endpoints compared; engraving placement excluded.
scope.ties: Tie-free truth is checked for extra XML sound/notation endpoints. Tie-bearing MuseScore truth is explicitly unsupported until a real fixture establishes its endpoint encoding.

qualification: Evidence for stated categories on this page only; this utility does not decide Audiveris-equivalent recognition quality.
